identity.real_world_identity_notes: This is a fictionalized Reiza generation/configuration. NASCAR history is context only; no real-world generation is inferred from the label.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed round rim without display or shift lights.

notes: Exact Superspeedway telemetry only; other Gen2 configurations are not aliases.
Four direct-selection H-pattern gears were verified.
Clutchless running shifts require throttle lift and manual blip; no automatic cut or blip was observed.

The downshift blip does not assert an unestablished construction here, and the reason is that this car has no real referent. For a car a simulator invented there is no real gearbox to be right or wrong about, so the simulator is the only authority that exists and its demand is the complete fact about the only version of this car there is. The dataset's rule - that `required` is reserved for gearboxes needing the blip to engage - governs claims about real cars and does not reach a record with no real car behind it. `required` stands as a known value.

That does not make the construction knowable. A required blip in AMS2 is not evidence of dog engagement: the simulator demands one on cars established as synchromesh, including both Formula Vee records and the Diablo SV-R. The demand establishes the technique the driver must use, not how the gearbox engages, so `gearbox_type` stays unknown here and would stay unknown even if this car were real.
Guided exact-configuration testing directly established every listed simulator behavior.

confidence.basis: Exact telemetry and guided behavior are verified; real-world generation mapping intentionally remains unresolved.

claims.basis: Official release and exact telemetry establish the fictionalized Gen2 Superspeedway identity.
Guided direct-selection and technique tests plus cockpit inspection establish exact configuration controls.
